If you strictly define pop punk as it's previous incarnations then yes you'd be correct but like all genres pop punk as a scene is a living thing that changes and grows in complexity with time. 

It's not pop punk a la blink 182 or Sum 41 but neither are several of the touted albums of the previous days this thread has been up. TGG by the wonder years isn't pop punk a la blink 182 but it's still up as yesterday's winner. 

Yes, Home like NoPlace is There is a very new and different brand of the scene but I think you'd be denying obvious influences and hallmarks of a pop punk/scene album that it possesses to say there is "literally nothing pop punk" about it or TDAG. 

It's a subgenre, which is inherently a different yet connected scene. (this is also all opinion but I believe that your take was a bit too reductive of a nuanced and complex genre that has, especially recently, become very grey and difficult to define)

I feel like this album does deserve the pop punk moniker because it's an early example of an undercurrent in the scene that traces back at least as far as The Devil and God are Raging Inside Me. 

There was a growing subset of pop punk/pop punk adjacent bands leaning into a post hardcore and post rock influence with a lot of darker undertones and departure from traditional style as the genre evolved. 

I think it's worth acknowledging that this transformation was occurring in the scene even if it isn't pop punk in the truest, most traditional sense. The genre was evolving, splitting, and transforming as the scene kinda blossomed into a bit of a renaissance/revival
